Diagnosis: The failure is caused by the reach_point constraint containing both manipulator_low_effort and manipulator_high_effort in the same stage. The runtime explicitly rejects conflicting manipulator effort conditions and requires exactly one expected effort condition for a single atomic action. Since this is a release/retract into free space, manipulator_low_effort is the appropriate expected condition; the unexpected high-effort safety stop cannot be represented simultaneously in this stage without triggering the validator conflict.
Reasoning: Use reach_point because the retract target is explicitly the estop_cap_tip origin offset by +0.10 m along estop_cap_tip +z, with a 0.01 m tolerance. freeze_orientation preserves the current panda_fingertip orientation throughout the retract, including the current tool +z and +y directions, without adding a new axis-alignment constraint. close_gripper keeps the fingers commanded closed during release/retract. Effort/contact monitoring is represented with manipulator_low_effort on the retract position term to require contact/effort to drop toward free-space during retraction. The alternative stop/inhibit condition for unexpected high effort is not included because the validator requires a single effort condition and rejects manipulator_high_effort together with manipulator_low_effort in one stage.
